notes: Read all four target units, full preceding Palestinian-demand context, all twelve candidates and the review. Disposed candidates one through six because they import earlier demands from context while citing the target's solidarity-call or authorship-credit units. Restored Palestinian speakers and beneficiaries to the resistance, repression, organizing and boycott demands; identified the solidarity recipient as Palestinians' freedom struggle; and resolved the process credit to the Palestinian-authored justice demands.

claims.claim_text: Palestinians in the United States demand the right to resist their oppression.
Palestinians in the United States demand the right to exercise assembly, dissent and speech without fear of political repression.
Palestinians in the United States should be free to organize their communities in pursuit of justice and liberation.
Palestinians in the United States demand an end to legislation they characterize as unconstitutional because it denies their right to boycott for human rights.
Palestinians in the United States call on people of conscience to support their freedom struggle and join their fight for collective liberation and justice for all.
The Palestinian-authored justice demands emerged through a process supported by the Adalah Justice Project and the US Campaign for Palestinian Rights.
